title: The Morning Digest: November 22, 2026
dek: Two more outbound tankers were struck near Khasab within an hour of each other on Saturday morning (UKMTO, Nov 21), three strikes in about fifteen hours, with no casualties, no closure and no confirmed cargo loss. Managed money WTI net length fell to +15,814 contracts, the lowest of 2026, after fresh shorts were added in the week to Nov 17 (CFTC, released Nov 20). Arabian Gulf loadings in January to October were down 27.6 percent year on year, with Fujairah and Yanbu, both outside the strait, now ahead of Ras Tanura (Banchero Costa, reported Nov 21). January WCS paper settled -$21.65 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 20). The validated diesel crack is $78.18 on the latest print.

sources.vintage: Nov 21, 2026 (an outbound tanker was struck on the stern by an unknown projectile about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab at 0500 UTC, and a second outbound tanker was struck in the engine room about 17 nautical miles east of Khasab at 0550 UTC; no casualties in either report; neither vessel named by UKMTO; with Friday's Warning 214-26 that is three Khasab-area strikes in about fifteen hours); NAVAREA IX Warning 457/26 via DeepDraft, Nov 22, 2026 (specialist reporting identifies one casualty as the TORKEL, reported burning and anchored; machinery state and any cargo loss unconfirmed); Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted area, an account Reuters could not verify, and UKMTO's word in both warnings is projectile; JMIC threat level for the strait remains SEVERE

Nov 20, 2026, positions as of Nov 17 (NYMEX WTI managed money net long +15,814, down 9,900 on the week and the lowest of 2026, at about 0.8 percent of open interest; longs rose 5,519 while shorts were added, up 15,419 to 137,797, the largest short book of the year; ICE Brent managed money net long +133,635, essentially flat after two flush weeks from a September peak of +282,657)

Nov 21, 2026 (Arabian Gulf crude loadings in January to October 2026 were 531.3 million tonnes, down 27.6 percent year on year; the Gulf share of global seaborne crude fell to 30.6 percent from 39.8 percent; Fujairah loaded 25.9 percent of Gulf loadings and Yanbu is second at 19.6 percent, both reachable without transiting Hormuz, ahead of Ras Tanura)
Nov 20, 2026 (Friday settles: Brent Jan27 $92.57, up $0.59, down 3.41 percent on the week, a third consecutive weekly loss; WTI Jan27 $83.41, up $0.97; the Brent prompt spread weakened on Friday)

Nov 22, 2026 (diesel crack $78.18 and 3-2-1 crack $39.86 on the latest print dated Nov 20; all time maximum diesel crack $117.92 on Sep 16; 45 total closes above $100; current streak above $100 is zero)

sources.publisher: Kpler media briefing via Associated Press
sources.vintage: Nov 18, 2026 (4d old) (crude flows through the strait itself were 8.5 million barrels a day in preliminary figures through Nov 16, about 50 percent of the pre-war level; oil moving by all routes out of the Middle East was 15.0 million barrels a day, about 64 percent of pre-war, down from 97 percent in October)

Nov 22, 2026 (12 commercial ships crossed on Nov 21, one of them a tanker; seven-day average 7.7 crossings a day against a pre-crisis 84.8 a day; AIS-visible only, ships running dark are not counted); Windward via thehormuzstrait.com, Nov 21, 2026 (16 crossings on Nov 20, seven of them dark)

Nov 22, 2026 (the Houthi military spokesperson warned shipping companies to remove vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports, naming Jeddah, Yanbu, Jazan and King Fahd Industrial Port as potential targets; no confirmed commercial vessel strike, no Saudi port closure and no mandatory evacuation order at the report's cutoff)

Nov 21, 2026 (the Sparta II, a United States-sanctioned, military-linked Russian cargo vessel, was hit by two drones in the Gulf of Finland, caught fire and drifted into Finnish waters; all 16 crew evacuated; no oil cargo involved and no export terminal hit)

Nov 18, 2026 (4d old) (Ukrainian drone attacks cut the Russian refinery run rate sharply from late October, with 15 of 35 major refineries disrupted or halted, while November average processing is still only 5 to 10 percent below September and October; seaborne crude exports averaged 3.9 million barrels a day in the four weeks to Nov 15)

sources.publisher: Iranian foreign minister interview in the state-run newspaper Iran, reported
sources.vintage: Nov 21, 2026 (Tehran has put forward a two-day framework to reopen Hormuz, Washington acting on day one and Iran reopening on day two; the Islamabad memorandum of understanding is no longer on the table; messages continue through Qatar and Pakistan; Washington has not accepted and gave no new statement on Nov 21 or 22)

Nov 21, 2026 (Saudi Arabia agreed to help replenish Japan's depleted crude stockpiles: Tokyo will buy up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude for its national petroleum reserve, and Riyadh gets temporary use of 16 million barrels of storage capacity in Japan on top of its existing 8 million barrel holding; Japan released reserves last month as part of an IEA-coordinated effort)

Nov 20, 2026 (Mars fell from a $10 premium to a $4 discount against WTI futures in less than a month; the pipeline carrying oil sands crude to West Coast export markets is operating at a record 960 kb/d this month, with 34 vessels scheduled out of Westridge in November against 31 in October)

Nov 20, 2026 (the North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption continued, with producers trucking Bakken crude to Dakota Access Pipeline delivery points, tanks filling and trucks in short supply; force majeure declarations stand at Flint Hills Pine Bend and at MPLX; no restart timeline has been published; the refinery receipt suspensions reported are of Bakken crude, and no WCS buyer outage was reported)

Nov 18, 2026 (standing reference) (December Mainline apportionment: Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert; the Cromer and Superior points for December were not retrievable in any public source on the Nov 22 check)

sources.publisher: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending
sources.vintage: Nov 13, 2026, released Nov 18, 2026 (4d old) (crude up 3.380 million barrels to 417.797 million; gasoline up 5.129 million; distillate up 1.571 million; Cushing down 1.209 million; refinery utilisation 95.7 percent; US production 14,032 kb/d; SPR down 3.174 million to 276.361 million, the lowest since August 1982)

Nov 21, 2026 (Rystad Energy's head of geopolitical analysis called the Nov 29 OPEC+ ministerial the much more important test, ahead of the December production hold; the meeting sets the 2027 framework and baselines off the independent capacity assessment completed Nov 17, whose figures remain unpublished)

Nov 20, 2026 (Alberta extended its carbon capture incentive program to 2035 and adjusted it so grants covering 12 percent of eligible capital costs can flow during construction; the Nov 15 target for definitive Pathways agreements passed with no announced deal)
Nov 20, 2026 (Western Canada oil-directed rigs fell nine to 153 in the week ended Nov 20, all nine in Alberta; gas-directed rigs rose three to 70; the national count stands at 231 total, oil 159)

sources.publisher: US Department of Energy, checked directly
sources.vintage: Nov 22, 2026 (no new solicitation, award announcement or posted contract change dated Nov 21 or 22 found; the newest DOE item is a Nov 20 grid emergency order; the latest SPR item remains the Oct 29 award completing the 172 million barrel programme)

sources.publisher: WCSB supply and demand balance build
sources.vintage: Nov 4, 2026 (standing reference) (AER ST3 actuals through September 2026: November supply about 192 kb/d and December about 216 kb/d above the proven egress bound of 4,541.6 kb/d, before the Nov 21 reconciled revision that moved December pipeline spare capacity by +60 kb/d; the balance residual is storage, and it is not carried as a storage forecast, because the traded strip tightening on volume with an orderly location spread and a record West Coast flow rate say the residual cannot be read that way; the error sits in one of two named suspects, either the production estimates are too high or the egress capacity is too low; carried forward and checked Nov 22, 2026)
